top.title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
top.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday. CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday. At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March. The post Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Mauricio Pochettino defends controversial Matthijs de Ligt call after Man Utd’s 4-0 Anfield humiliation by Liverpool
top.description: FBL-ENG-PR-LIVERPOOL-MAN UTD - AFP Mauricio Pochettino has defended his eyebrow-raising decision to throw Matthijs de Ligt straight into Manchester United’s starting XI for his debut in charge during a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. The new Red Devils boss explained why he handed the Dutchman his first Premier League start in nearly a year. Pochettino stands by De Ligt selection The Dutch international had not featured in the league for 357 days due to a long-term back injury, yet found himself thrown into the heat of a North West derby . United’s defensive frailties were exposed almost immediately when De Ligt misjudged a long ball, allowing Alexander Isak to sprint through on goal. This error forced Leny Yoro into the desperate challenge that led to his dismissal. Goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz soon followed, before Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout in the second half. Despite the defender appearing slow and lethargic as he struggled with the pace of the game, Pochettino defended the selection following the final whistle. "He was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty. I think when we arrived, we saw the combination [with Lisandro Martinez]," Pochettino told Sky Sports . Furious boss slams refereeing double standards The game-changing decision left Pochettino absolutely seething, with the manager quick to highlight a glaring double standard in the officiating following an earlier, unpunished penalty shout involving Jeremy Jacquet. Convinced that the referee's inconsistency completely altered the complexion of the match, Pochettino didn't hold back in his post-match assessment. "And I repeat again, Jacquet was a penalty, and if the referee says that is a penalty, for sure that action after never comes, and maybe we talk in another way," a frustrated Pochettino declared. "One centre-back made a mistake, was penalty, wasn't punished, and us, we made one mistake and we were punished. Now I accept all the situation, but the circumstances are the circumstances. It's so important to put the circumstance in front. Always." Reality check for new regime The defeat extends United’s winless streak in the Premier League to nine matches, marking the club's worst-ever run in the competition's history. Pochettino was seen in deep discussion with the officiating crew after the game, though he admitted that his protests would do little to change the outcome of his first match in charge. He emphasized the need for his squad to take responsibility for their performance while remaining critical of the external factors that influenced the game. "I have to defend my club," the Argentine coach stated. "And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card." top.description: LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - NOVEMBER 13: Mark Pope the head coach oof the Kentucky Wildcats gives instructions to his team against the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks at Rupp Arena on November 13, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images KenPom projections aren’t the be-all, end-all of college basketball, and plenty of teams have made Ken Pomeroy’s algorithm look foolish by the time March rolls around. At the same time, his numbers aren’t something you can simply shrug off and pretend don’t exist either. When a model that tracks every single possession in Division I basketball starts flashing bright red warning lights, it is usually telling you something you already saw with your own eyes. Following Friday night’s 90-76 loss to Indiana in Indianapolis, KenPom released its latest update, and it is the last thing Big Blue Nation wanted to see. Breaking down Kentucky’s latest KenPom numbers Coming into the 2026-27 season, Kentucky sat just outside the KenPom preseason top 25 at No. 26. After early stumbles against Kansas and a narrow escape against Northern Arizona, the Wildcats had already tumbled outside the top 50. The 14-point defeat to the Hoosiers only accelerated the freefall. They are now No. 63 overall, No. 24 in adjusted offense and 131 in adjusted defense. The projected record is now sitting at 16-16 (6-12). That would be a disaster, much like Kentucky’s defense. The Cats can’t keep anyone out of the lane and are almost always in a rotation. And yet, the same defense keeps getting trotted out. Maybe try a zone? It surely couldn’t be much worse. The headline number that hurts the most As ugly as a 16-16 overall projection looks on paper, the real gut punch shows up when you scroll through the game-by-game forecast. Right now, KenPom projects Kentucky to be favored in just one SEC game : South Carolina. Kentucky is projected to be favored in just one SEC game, according to KenPom. pic.twitter.com/fMFy3SUIiN — Jeff Borzello (@jeffborzello) November 21, 2026 Out of an 18-game conference slate, the Wildcats are currently projected as the underdog in 17 of them. Reality vs. the numbers Now, let’s keep some perspective. too. Kentucky is going to win more than one SEC game, and they will probably win more than 8. Basketball isn’t played on a spreadsheet, and even KenPom’s own math agrees, which is why the overall forecast still pegs the Wildcats for a 6-12 conference finish rather than 1-17. Over the course of an 18-game grind, teams steal road games, catch fire at Rupp Arena, and pull off upsets. But the fact that Kentucky could enter almost every single conference game as the underdog is not something that should ever be uttered. top.title: Patriots expected to show interest in Daniel Jones, but there’s a catch
top.description: With their season at a crossroads in light of the fractured fibula suffered by starting quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots are exploring the possibility of adding another passer to the mix. One name to keep an eye on is Daniel Jones, who was let go by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday . Jones, 29, was placed on waivers, meaning that any team has the opportunity to claim him. However, according to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, that is not expected to happen. And once he makes it through the wire and to the open market, the Patriots are among the teams expected to take a look at him. “The Patriots along with the Baltimore Ravens and maybe the Arizona Cardinals are expected to have interest in the recently-waived former Colts starter,” Rapoport said on the air on Sunday. “He goes on waivers. We find out 4 p.m. on Monday whether or not anyone claims him. Unlikely because of the $2 million due this year, $10 million guaranteed for injury next year.” With Maye potentially missing the next six weeks , if not more, the Patriots are looking at a starter-backup combination of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Adding Jones to the mix would therefore make sense given his experience in the NFL and the fact that he has played some winning football previously in his career. However, there is a catch: the former first-round draft pick appears to be willing to wait for the right opportunity to come along. “If he clears [waivers], my understanding is that Daniel Jones is expected to wait,” Rapoport said. “Just to wait, see if there’s another quarterback injury. Of course, if there was, he would be the first call of any playoff team needing a quarterback.” If Jones is indeed in no rush to sign with a team, the Patriots’ interest might just start to evaporate. At 5-5 and the current eighth playoff seed in the AFC, they simply might not have time to wait for Jones. Instead, they might just try their luck with DeVito — who is in his second year in the system — rather than try to bring Jones aboard late and then try to get him up to starter-caliber speed. The Patriots, with DeVito currently atop their quarterback depth chart, will visit the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12.

The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods. Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira. Traders trying to salvage what is left after the fire One of the affected traders, Usman Sani, recounted how the fire spread through the market, destroying shops and goods before traders could salvage their belongings. “We received the news of the fire and rushed to the market, but by the time we got here, the flames had already spread. Many shops were affected, and traders lost goods worth millions of naira. The situation is heartbreaking,” he said. top.title: OKC nail artist's TikTok went viral. Now she does Jared McCain's nails
top.description: When Jared McCain was traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder, Yvie McCrary saw more than basketball news. She saw a potential client. The Oklahoma City nail artist took her shot on TikTok, posting a video in hopes of catching McCain's attention. It went viral. He saw it. And soon, the NBA guard known for his elaborate manicures was sitting at McCrary's nail table. Months later, McCrary painted McCain's nails gold for Thunder media day . When he flashed them to The Oklahoman during a news conference, video of the manicure generated more than a million views on the NBA's social account. It was quite a leap for an artist barely three years into her career. And another sign of how nail art, long coded as feminine, is finding an increasingly visible place in men's fashion, including among professional athletes. McCain first found an interest in nail artistry during the COVID-19 pandemic, in his early years of high school. With nothing to do at home, he saw others do it online and decided to give it a try. "I liked the way it looked, and it became a unique part of something that I do, and now it's just part of me," McCain told The Oklahoman during OKC Thunder media day. Before he was playing professional basketball, he was already finding ways to bring nail art onto the court. During the basketball playoffs in high school, McCain painted his nails with the logo of each team his team defeated. By the time they won the championship, all five fingers represented stops along the title run. The hobby followed McCain to the NBA. He was drafted by the Philadelphia 76ers in the 2024 NBA Draft and later traded to Oklahoma City in February 2026. It has also become part of his brand. In a sports world filled with Nike, Adidas and Jordan partnerships, McCain has a deal with nail polish brand Sally Hansen. top.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
top.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

nigeria.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday. CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday. At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. nigeria.title: Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks
nigeria.description: The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement. The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP. Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough. – Political ‘boycotts’ – On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government. Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition. Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government. The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail. The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies. It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”. For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus. “Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme. Bowen identified the same issue. “The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said. “That’s a very tough ask.” ‘Significant reform’ COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.” But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms. He described that as a “particular challenge,” although others might characterise it as simply impossible. nigeria.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
nigeria.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats. “House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X. Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount. Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.” “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X. The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability

He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. sports.title: Patriots expected to show interest in Daniel Jones, but there’s a catch
sports.description: With their season at a crossroads in light of the fractured fibula suffered by starting quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots are exploring the possibility of adding another passer to the mix. One name to keep an eye on is Daniel Jones, who was let go by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday . Jones, 29, was placed on waivers, meaning that any team has the opportunity to claim him. However, according to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, that is not expected to happen. And once he makes it through the wire and to the open market, the Patriots are among the teams expected to take a look at him. “The Patriots along with the Baltimore Ravens and maybe the Arizona Cardinals are expected to have interest in the recently-waived former Colts starter,” Rapoport said on the air on Sunday. “He goes on waivers. We find out 4 p.m. on Monday whether or not anyone claims him. Unlikely because of the $2 million due this year, $10 million guaranteed for injury next year.” With Maye potentially missing the next six weeks , if not more, the Patriots are looking at a starter-backup combination of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Adding Jones to the mix would therefore make sense given his experience in the NFL and the fact that he has played some winning football previously in his career. However, there is a catch: the former first-round draft pick appears to be willing to wait for the right opportunity to come along. “If he clears [waivers], my understanding is that Daniel Jones is expected to wait,” Rapoport said. “Just to wait, see if there’s another quarterback injury. Of course, if there was, he would be the first call of any playoff team needing a quarterback.” If Jones is indeed in no rush to sign with a team, the Patriots’ interest might just start to evaporate. At 5-5 and the current eighth playoff seed in the AFC, they simply might not have time to wait for Jones. Instead, they might just try their luck with DeVito — who is in his second year in the system — rather than try to bring Jones aboard late and then try to get him up to starter-caliber speed. The Patriots, with DeVito currently atop their quarterback depth chart, will visit the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12.

sports.title: OKC nail artist's TikTok went viral. Now she does Jared McCain's nails
sports.description: When Jared McCain was traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder, Yvie McCrary saw more than basketball news. She saw a potential client. The Oklahoma City nail artist took her shot on TikTok, posting a video in hopes of catching McCain's attention. It went viral. He saw it. And soon, the NBA guard known for his elaborate manicures was sitting at McCrary's nail table. Months later, McCrary painted McCain's nails gold for Thunder media day . When he flashed them to The Oklahoman during a news conference, video of the manicure generated more than a million views on the NBA's social account. It was quite a leap for an artist barely three years into her career. And another sign of how nail art, long coded as feminine, is finding an increasingly visible place in men's fashion, including among professional athletes. McCain first found an interest in nail artistry during the COVID-19 pandemic, in his early years of high school. With nothing to do at home, he saw others do it online and decided to give it a try. "I liked the way it looked, and it became a unique part of something that I do, and now it's just part of me," McCain told The Oklahoman during OKC Thunder media day. Before he was playing professional basketball, he was already finding ways to bring nail art onto the court. During the basketball playoffs in high school, McCain painted his nails with the logo of each team his team defeated. By the time they won the championship, all five fingers represented stops along the title run. The hobby followed McCain to the NBA. He was drafted by the Philadelphia 76ers in the 2024 NBA Draft and later traded to Oklahoma City in February 2026. It has also become part of his brand. In a sports world filled with Nike, Adidas and Jordan partnerships, McCain has a deal with nail polish brand Sally Hansen. But when McCain arrived in Oklahoma City, he still needed someone to actually do his nails. That's where McCrary came in. OKC nail artist shoots her shot McCrary had just celebrated her two-year "nail birthday," as she calls it, when she learned McCain was headed to Oklahoma City. McCrary posted a TikTok for fun, with hopes of getting the shooting guard's attention, and after the video went viral, it landed on McCain’s feed. "He messaged me and wanted to come get nails; that was pretty cool for me," McCrary said. McCrary started cosmetology school in 2022, dreaming of becoming a hair stylist, but as part of the course, she needed to take a nail class. McCrary didn't think she was going to like it at first, but fell in love with the art once she got into it. "It's so versatile," McCrary said. "You can get pretty creative with it. ... A lot of people get single colors or clean girl nails and I'm like, 'Nope!' I like all the art; I like to do all the crazy fun things." sports.description: Motorsport photo In one of those curious twists of fate, Marquez sealed his eighth MotoGP world title at Portimo just as Rossi was touring Italy to promote his autobiography, La Mia Storia , which was released on 10 November. Throughout those appearances, mainly on television and radio programmes, references to Marquez were a constant feature, subsequently picked up and amplified by the media. Not only by the specialist publications, but also by plenty of others with little connection to motorcycle racing, unwilling to pass up the opportunity to cash in on some particularly lucrative clicks. As for the substance of Rossi's message, there was nothing new: he was simply reiterating his long-held views on Marquez. The same views he has repeated for the past 11 years, ever since the 'Sepang Clash', the incident that forever divided the motorcycling world into Rossi and Marquez camps, and about which far too much has already been said and written. Ever since the Spaniard burst onto the MotoGP scene like a thunderbolt in 2013, he has been competing with the Italian for just about everything. On the track, for points, victories and titles. Off it, for the right to occupy the throne reserved for the rider regarded as the GOAT – the greatest of all time. That particular contest is impossible to settle if statistics – which now favour Marquez – are taken out of the equation, because any judgement is entirely subjective, shaped by personal opinions, admiration and allegiances towards either rider. With Rossi having retired five years ago and Marquez still winning, if there is one thing that continues to set them against each other, it is the narrative. Or, more precisely, the way that narrative is manipulated. As 'The Doctor' himself has acknowledged in recent days, he has still not recovered from the bitter disappointment of 2015. "It's something that doesn't go away; it still hurts. More than 10 years have passed, but the feeling and my state of mind when I think back to it are exactly the same as they were that night in Valencia, and that worries me a little," he admitted just a few days ago, during one of his many promotional appearances. It was a disappointment which, it is worth remembering, came after Rossi had pursued a disastrous strategy, seemingly devised by his worst enemy or, at the very least, by someone with a remarkable lack of judgement. The plan succeeded in reawakening a Marquez who had nothing left to play for in a championship that had already become an exclusively Yamaha affair. sports.title: Ravens drop 6th straight to Panthers, put season on life support
sports.description: The Baltimore Ravens dropped their sixth straight game in a rollicking, back-and-forth 35-33 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon. After a wild 58 minutes that included seven lead changes and no less than a dozen jaw-dropping plays, Carolina took the lead on a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal with 1:47 to go. Baltimore’s potential game-winning drive was snuffed out by a Jacoby Brissett interception, and the Ravens dropped to 4-7 . The currently sit 11th in the AFC – and in the 2027 draft order. That is starting to sound like a good thing for a team that should be considering major changes this offseason. The Ravens defense gave up the lead four different times on Sunday afternoon, including twice directly after scores from the offense. The offense turned the ball over twice and gained just eight yards across their first three drives of the second half. And outside of a Devontez Walker kickoff return touchdown, Baltimore’s special teams units struggled with sloppy ball-handling and poor coverage. And yet, the Ravens had two distinct chances to win this game late in the fourth quarter. The first was the Panthers’ penultimate drive, in which Baltimore’s defense could not dig their heels in and protect a one-point lead. Brissett’s gunslinging on the previous drive showed he was capable of driving into field goal range, but another collapse in pass protection forced him to throw a prayer out of bounds to avoid a sack. Except the pass did not make it to the sidelines, instead landing in the arms of Panthers linebacker Tyrel Dodson. In both instances, the Ravens could not be at their best when their best was needed. Despite thrilling wins over the Cowboys and Falcons, first-year head coach Jesse Minter’s oft-repeated mantra never fully took root in The Castle. And it is fair to question if he has lived up to his own standard. Brissett was rushing partially because Minter declined to take a timeout after a sack with 1:30 to go. 24 seconds later, Brissett threw a checkdown to Justice Hill to set up a 4th-and-1. Only then did Minter stop the clock, only for Brissett to restart it with a sneak that chewed up another 23 seconds before the pick. This is the second game in a row that Minter’s questionable timeout usage has costed the Ravens precious time in end-of-half situations – two contests that were decided by a total of five points. At the end of the day, the coaching staff is failing simple math problems – and struggling to keep their finger on the pulse of the game. To be fair, that pulse was all over the play. To borrow a phrase from a Saturday Night Live great, this game had everything: a replay-assisted safety; a wildcat flea flicker touchdown; a fumble out of the end zone, a muffed punt, and Walker’s return touchdown – all from the Ravens, all in the first 20 minutes. sports.title: Giants QB Jameis Winston restrains teammate Malik Nabers during angry moment on the touchline
sports.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images New York Giants QB Jameis Winston’s veteran instincts kicked in during a heated moment involving 23-year-old WR Malik Nabers during their 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Giants are proving to be more competitive than many had assumed before the season, with their 6-3-1 record putting them in pole position to secure the NFC East and a spot in the playoffs one season after going 4-13. One of the key reasons for this turnaround has been WR Nabers, who tore his ACL last season. While Nabers is impressing fans on the field with his raw prowess and route-running skills, he also needs to ensure he stays level-headed and focused on winning. Malik Nabers needed to be calmed down by Jameis Winston during Giants win With under six minutes left in this closely poised contest, Nabers was visibly upset on the touchline when the Giants’ defence was on the field, with backup QB Winston restraining the young WR. This situation has since been downplayed, as neither Nabers nor Winston had anything negative to say about the seemingly tense confrontation. Nabers claims to have just been saying he was good while passionately cheering the defence on from the touchline. It seems to be a moment of excessive passion flowing out in the middle of a close game between two teams that hope to make runs in the playoffs. Nabers went 7/12 on receptions for 55 yards and one touchdown in this game. He has gone 65/97 all season for 747 receiving yards and three TDs. He is looking like he’s back to peak fitness and willing to do anything to help the Giants add to their win column. Winston was the Giants’ starting QB earlier this season after Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the season after Week 2. He has since transitioned into a backup/mentor role after the team acquired former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings. The passion on display from Nabers and the leadership from Winston both are great signs for a once-proud franchise hoping to become a competitive force again. technology.title: Old-school Linux desktops find fresh routes to Wayland
technology.description: Xfce's next release is taking shape for 2027, while MATE users have fresh options for moving their familiar desktop onto Wayland. One of the oldest surviving Linux desktops has a relatively slow release schedule: new stable releases of Xfce tend to appear every two years. The project just updated its release engineering roadmap for the forthcoming Xfce 4.22, and it looks like the next version won't arrive until early next year. We covered the release of Xfce 4.20 in December 2024, but 4.22 is still incubating. The roadmap schedules its first prerelease and feature freeze for December 15, 2026, followed by a second prerelease on January 15, 2027. A third prerelease is optional, and neither that nor the final release has a date. February or March might be plausible, but that's our guess, not the project's promise. The Xfce developers tend not to rush into things. Wayland development continues in 4.22, building on the preliminary support in 4.20. The team is also working on its own compositor, xfwl4, although the roadmap doesn't promise feature parity with X11. (In Wayland terminology, the "compositor" is the combined display server and window manager.) The compositor has its own development roadmap . The name is a nod to the current Xfce X11 window manager, which is called xfwm4 . The main developer of the new xfwl4 compositor is Brian Tarricone , who has been working on other parts of Xfce since 2004. Back in July, he shared a blog post about his use of generative-AI coding assistants called LLMs and xfwl4 . He says: "So yes, I use Claude quite a bit while developing xfwl4. I don't vibe-code, ever, and I probably use the LLM to generate less code than most people do. After all, building things with code is my hobby and passion (and I'm lucky I got to do it professionally for a quarter century), and driving an LLM is kinda boring." We find this somewhat reassuring, but any really passionate anti-LLM Xfce users reading this may be glad that the release schedules of Ubuntu LTS versions and Xfce stable releases are so far out of sync – sticking with Xubuntu 26.04 means there's no immediate need to adopt the new LLM-assisted compositor. Or, of course, simply keep using X11 instead of Wayland – although that might eventually mean choosing a distro that maintains X11 support, perhaps through XLibre, which has other drawbacks for some. There are other options, too. We've also seen an independent fork of xfwm4 called xfwm4-gl . It's in active development and uses OpenGL to perform window compositing directly, while the current version uses the now rather old Xrender extension . technology.title: Airbus may be leaving Microsoft Office, but for its 36,000 defense staff, Office isn't leaving them
technology.description: Airbus has a plan to phase out Microsoft Office, but about 22 percent of its roughly 165,000 employees will stay on it because their sensitive data must remain on-premise. In March 2018, Airbus signed a contract with Google to move its workforce - 130,000 strong at that time - onto the cloud-based Workspace suite. Years later, compatibility issues mean some users still need Excel. Catherine Jestin, Airbus's executive vice president of digital, told The Register that Google is still working to resolve software interface conflicts between departments and improve features. Last year, for example, Google tripled the number of cells available in Sheets, which let Airbus "reduce significantly the number of users on Microsoft." This year, Google improved the compatibility of document watermarking. Contracts, for instance, are often exported from Excel to Sheets by one department, edited by another, and sent back. "Sometimes we had compatibility issues when you were commenting, the comments were lost, or they were not transferable in one way or the other," she said. "Now they [Google] have made it totally compatible, which means that it makes it much easier for us to decommission people working on contracts… the legal department, the sales department, purchasing department, making it much easier to have that internal collaboration." Airbus and Google have a roadmap to eliminate Microsoft Office. Jestin expects the migration to finish in "another two to three years." Not every part of the company will switch. The Defence division , which accounts for the 22 percent (more than 36,000 people), will keep using classic Microsoft Office. "We will not get 100 percent out of Microsoft because again, for the defense industry people, they cannot [use] Microsoft Office 365 or Google Workspace, they have to stay on-premise, and the only solution that is available on-premise is Microsoft. So Microsoft Office will remain for colleagues who are working in the defense and space programs." As we pointed out a year ago, kicking the Microsoft habit is no easy feat. ®

technology.title: When Microsoft, Apple, and the FAA can't keep it up, it's a system of a down
technology.description: No Access November is going well this year. Among the many organizations to adopt Outage As A Service (OAAS) were Microsoft , Apple , the FAA , and any number of European supermarkets . Even the NSA has succumbed. For us, at least, outage is word of the year. It's certainly deeply embedded in the public mind, with schoolchildren reportedly referring to the 19th century Irish famine as "the potato outage." There's no danger of an outrage outage. OAAS is synonymous with infrastructure failure, a more useful term that begins to hint at cause and cure as well as effect. In all of the latest crop, what we know is depressingly familiar. Microsoft's O365 meltdown was a cascading failure caused by a botched upgrade that took stuff offline and melted down as it tried to come back. The FAA was a migration from Jurassic hardware that wasn't end of life so much as living fossil. The Eurofridge-cum-fondue-maker was a control system so badly written it fell apart if you raised an eyebrow at it. Clearly, nobody had. Until now. These are all different classes of OAAS that have been around for decades. Security-based outages are still outages, and a packet flood is still a packet flood whether it's a botnet DDoS or finger trouble in the config dashboard. Each of them has a root cause with obvious fixes – a faulty mental model of network/server interaction, chronic underfunding, a complete supply chain with little cyber-security expertise. All these, like the poor, will be with us always. They won't fix themselves. Infrastructure that works is invisible, and invisible things are forgotten until they break. What's needed is an infrastructure that watches itself, that is designed to be adaptive and resilient, one that refuses to connect to danger and nulls out any that gets through. There have been attempts to create a ground-up architecture that is inherently risk resistant. One such is SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks). It redesigns routing between domains around explicit path selection, separate control and data planes, and mechanisms for trust and failure isolation. The result is a very resilient, very reliable, and very secure infrastructure that reflects the designers' tenet that you can't patch the internet into any of these things. Start from scratch or GTFO. SCION started about 15 years ago, and it works well enough to be adopted by entities like the Secure Swiss Finance Network . If the Gnomes of Zurich trust it, no higher accreditation exists. Well, it was designed by ETH Zürich. Where you won't find it is almost everywhere else. The internet is like Switzerland in the same way the Amazon rainforest is like Central Park. There are trees and sometimes it rains. It is unwise to infer anything else. Given you can't manicure existing infrastructure into true resilience, the only other option is evolution. technology.title: Software issues have even reached Mercury as BepiColombo probe arrives in uncertain state
technology.description: Humanity’s third-ever mission to Mercury has arrived, but a last-minute “software issue” has complicated matters. The BepiColombo mission is a joint effort by the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Reaching Mercury is not easy because its gravity is weak and its orbit is fast. The tiny planet’s proximity to the Sun further complicates matters, because our star’s gravity accelerates everything that falls towards it. BepiColombo’s journey has therefore seen it whiz past Earth once, Venus twice, and Mercury six times on a complicated path the two space agencies designed to slow it down sufficiently to be captured by mercurial gravity, while also keeping up with its rapid orbit. In 2024, the craft’s thrusters underperformed, leading the ESA and JAXA to re-plot the planned trajectory and reschedule its arrival at Mercury from mid-2025 to this past weekend. The ESA’s operations team sent the commands to insert BepiColombo into orbit on Friday. On Sunday the craft phoned home with news that it entered orbit. A little later, however, the ESA revealed “the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue.” The spacecraft is safe, but the ESA says it is “working to understand what happened” and promised updates early this week. Readers may recall that a pair of NASA missions to Mars are also experiencing software glitches , which have in recent weeks become all-too-prevalent on Earth, too. Fingers crossed If all is well, BepiColombo will deploy two orbiters. The ESA’s craft is called the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), which the ESA says will map the planet, assess the composition of its surface and interior, measure its magnetic field, and even gather data that scientists hope will “test Einstein's theory of General Relativity to an unprecedented level of accuracy.” JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO) will also investigate the planet’s magnetic field, plasma, dust, and atmosphere. Both orbiters are extraordinary feats of engineering. As JAXA explains , MIO is solar-powered but the sunlight it will receive at Mercury is around ten times as powerful as on Earth. Mercury itself is also sufficiently hot that the orbiter needs protection from heat radiated from the planet’s surface. ESA’s MPO keeps itself cool with three to four insulating blankets comprised of layered titanium, aluminum, and a ceramic fabric called Nextel. The blankets alone weigh 94kg. The two space agencies expect to start science operations in April 2027 but haven’t yet said if the two orbiters are in peak condition. JAXA, sadly, last week revealed that its Hayabusa2 probe has deteriorated to the point at which it can no longer make its planned landing on asteroid 1998 KY26. JAXA scheduled that for the year 2031, but problems with the probe’s thrusters mean the agency will instead attempt a high-speed fly-by of asteroid 2015 BM510 in 2028. technology.title: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
technology.description: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago. The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going." Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables. He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register . Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test. "I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair." Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email. "Ha-ha, very funny." Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email. "It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to." What a coincidence! Or maybe not? "It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was." Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

technology.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
technology.description: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. technology.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. science.title: Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites postponed due to a technical issue
science.description: null Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft has been postponed due to a technical issue. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation was scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Monday (Nov. 23). However, the countdown was halted following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . The countdown was stopped before the removal of the mobile gantry, with Arianespace confirming that the rocket and its satellite payload remain safe and stable. Technical teams are now assessing the issue, with the next launch opportunity no earlier than Tuesday (Nov. 24). The launch will be streamed live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, once a new launch date and time have been confirmed. Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The upcoming mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year. science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together.
